{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   -n 4
#   --mem 4096 (MB)
#   -p mhigh,mhigh
#   --gres gpu:1
#   -o logs/%x_%u_%j.out
#   -e logs/%x_%u_%j.err

flux alloc \
  -n 4 \
  --gpus=1 \
  --queue=mhigh \
  bash -lc '

mkdir -p logs

# NOTE: Slurm --mem 4096 has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, the job may be placed where less memory is available,
# increasing risk of OOM or contention.

# NOTE: Slurm partition list "-p mhigh,mhigh" (fallback partitions) has no portable Flux equivalent.
# We select the first listed queue (mhigh).
# Performance implication: if that queue is busy/unavailable, queue wait time may increase.

# NOTE: Slurm output pattern uses %x (job name), %u (user), %j (job id). Flux has no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but log naming/organization may be degraded.
# Best-effort: use script name as jobname, $USER, and Flux job id.
exec >"logs/task_b_${USER}_${FLUX_JOB_ID}.out" \
     2>"logs/task_b_${USER}_${FLUX_JOB_ID}.err"

python task_b.py \
    --loss "triplet" \
    --miner "BatchHard" \
    --output_path "outputs_task_c/" \
    --dataset "mit_split" \
    --dataset_config_path "./configs/mit_split.yaml" \
    --dataset_path "/home/mcv/datasets/MIT_split/" \
    --model resnet_18 \
    --embedding_size 256 \
    --batch_size 64 \
    --epochs 20
'
"
}
